transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Grant (Redwood AE), Nina Romero (Redwood SE), Tobias Nguyen (Redwood Product), Dr. Aisha Khan (Polaris ML Lead), Ethan Park (Polaris Eng Mgr), Ravi Mehta (Polaris CTO), Maya Singh (Polaris Privacy)
---
SUMMARY: Quick console-driven walkthrough of Redwood Optimize for quantization profiles. Focus on INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, latency/fidelity curves, recommended rollout plan and pilot next steps. Discussed compliance and perf benchmarking windows.
TOPICS (auto): Optimize demo, qprofile creation, console playback, latency vs quality graphs, fallback policies, pilot scope
---
00:00 Lucas: okay everybody, thanks for joining. we, uh, we should have about 45 minutes. agenda is quick refresher on Optimize, then a live console demonstration of qprofiles — int8 and fp8 — and then tradeoffs and a pilot plan. Nina will drive the demo.
00:22 Nina: hey team, hi Aisha, Ethan, Ravi — thanks for taking time. Quick note, apologies in advance for any auto-caption weirdness. i'll show three profile presets we typically use: conservative, balanced, and throughput.
00:40 Aisha: sounds good, quick question — we care a lot about latency at tail, but also no hallucination on clinical notes. is there a way to tune for both?
00:53 Nina: yes. in the console Optimize tab you can attach a qprofile to a route; our qprofiles are layered — they specify quant format, activation calibrations and sensitivity thresholds. for example FP8-balanced will target fp8 kernels with per-layer outlier clamping; int8-throughput will use per-channel symmetric quant and more aggressive clipping.
01:12 Ethan: sorry can you slow down, when you say clip, does that change token-level probabilities?
01:20 Nina: it can. clipping and per-layer calibration change representation, so you might see subtle shifts in logit magnitudes. that sometimes manifests as small top-1 differences, more on longer sequences.
01:37 Tobias: quick product note: we also provide a fidelity lane graph comparing BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy metrics and a human-rated fidelity score when you upload labelled sets.
01:50 Ravi: is the fidelity score generated on-host or in Redwood cloud? privacy is a concern for us.
01:57 Lucas: good call — default demo uses Redwood sandbox but for Polaris we can run the evals inside your VPC under Redwood Private. Maya, that was a topic you wanted right?
02:10 Maya: yes, we need KMS integration and proof of no-persist logs for PII. will want SOC2 docs too.
02:18 Lucas: we'll attach SOC2 + network diagram after the call.
02:21 Nina: back to console — opening Optimize > Profiles. i have three presets loaded for this account. i'm going to run a playback of the latency vs fidelity sweep we did last month — note this is synthetic but representative.
02:40 [screen share: console UI loads, small stutter]
02:47 Nina: top chart is median latency per token, bottom chart is fidelity delta vs baseline FP16. baseline here is unconstrained FP16 at ~1.2x cost. you can see int8-throughput drops median latency by ~38% but fidelity delta is -5 to -9% on our clinical summarization prompts. FP8-balanced sits in between at -18% latency and -2 to -4% fidelity.
03:15 Aisha: that -9% sounds scary — is that on hallucination or just rouge?
03:22 Nina: mostly automated metrics here; for hallucination we ran a targeted eval — the hallucination rate uptick with int8 was concentrated on long-chain referencing tasks, not short discharge notes. we flagged prompts where d.o.p (degree of perturbation) was highest.
03:40 Ethan: are these numbers reproducible on our infra? we use 32k context and our sequences average 4k tokens for summaries.
03:48 Nina: good question — numbers shift with seq length. our kernels and KV cache behavior make int8 more sensitive with large KV cache usage. I will create a custom qprofile that keeps KV cache in fp16 while quantizing the weights to int8 — that hybrid can recover much of the fidelity at a modest latency cost.
04:10 Lucas: that's exactly one of the middle-ground strategies — hybrid FP16-KV + int8 weights. we call it weight-only quant in some docs, but console labels it as hybrid-kv-safe.
04:24 Tobias: showing the console 'sensitivity heatmap' — a per-layer contribution to fidelity loss. you can pin layers as fp16 to avoid regressions.
04:35 Aisha: so operationally what would you recommend for a pilot? roll out int8 to a tiny percentage then evaluate?
04:43 Nina: recommended pilot: 1) start with FP8-balanced on 5% of traffic for 2 weeks with the three prompt buckets; 2) run labeled fidelity eval on the same timeframe; 3) if pass, step to int8-throughput on 1% for stress testing and keep hybrid-kv for long sequences.
05:02 Ravi: and what about cost delta? how much we saving per token?
05:08 Nina: approximate — FP8 typically saves 18-25% cost relative to FP16 on our hosted fleet; int8 can be 35-50% depending on batching and kernel availability. big caveat: if you need to pin many layers to fp16, int8 saving shrinks.
05:24 Ethan: what about tail latency percentiles? 95th and 99th are critical for our UI.
05:31 Nina: we instrument p95 and p99 — int8 has slightly lower median but p99 can be more variable if there's cache thrash. our console shows per-route p95/p99; Optimize suggests autoscale and burst slots to protect p99.
05:48 [15 seconds of cross talk about screen]
06:05 Nina: i'm going to run a quick live sample — same prompt set: a 2.5k token discharge summary. you'll see side-by-side outputs: baseline(fp16) vs fp8-balanced vs int8-throughput.
06:22 [playback starts — text rendering on screen]
06:30 Aisha: hm first glance fp8 looks fine, int8 has a missing medication mention — looks like an extraction miss.
06:36 Nina: yeah that's the kind of token-level shift I mentioned; for extraction tasks we often pin the final decoder layer to fp16, that mitigates missing spans.
06:47 Ethan: can the console auto-suggest pins?
06:50 Nina: yes, Optimize has an 'auto-pin' button based on sensitivity thresholds. it suggests a minimal set of layers to keep in fp16. you can accept suggestions or tweak manually.
07:05 Tobias: note that auto-pin is conservative to avoid false negatives; you can set sensitivity to aggressive to push for more savings but with higher risk.
07:18 Aisha: show me the audit trail for changes — we need RBAC and change logs.
07:23 Lucas: Console -> Deployments -> History holds the rollout entries; each release captures qprofile id, who approved, and diff of layer pins. RBAC integrates with SAML so only admins can accept auto-pin changes.
07:38 Maya: do we have an SLA if an int8 rollout causes fidelity regressions in production?
07:43 Lucas: standard Dedicated customers get rollback policies and faster scale; for Private we can configure automatic fallback to baseline model on anomaly detection. part of pilot we configure rollback thresholds.
07:54 Ethan: can we do an on-prem eval inside our cluster, or does Redwood need to host?
07:58 Nina: we can run the Optimize eval tooling inside your VPC. Redwood Private includes the eval runner that posts only metric aggregates back to Redwood control plane; nothing persistent.
08:12 Aisha: what about temperature/randomness differences across quant formats? we get subtle prompted style shifts.
08:18 Nina: quant can change logits distribution; we recommend re-calibrating temperature and sampling settings per qprofile — Optimize has a 'sampling replay' tool to compare token distributions.
08:30 Ravi: ok how long to set up a pilot? how much engineering time?
08:34 Lucas: minimal Redwood-side: 2-3 engineering touch points to set up VPC access and eval runner, plus one session for qprofile tuning. Polaris side: provide prompt sets, test data and a small infra window for benchmarking. end-to-end around 2 weeks for initial pass.
08:53 Nina: i'm going to open the pilot worksheet - you'll see suggested buckets: extraction, summarization short, summarization long. each bucket maps to expected thresholds.
09:06 [screen: pilot worksheet visible]
09:12 Nina: for extraction we expect fidelity tolerance of <=1% top-1 token drift; for long summarization tolerance is higher. these are configurable per-bucket.
09:25 Aisha: can we include hallucination-specific tests? we have a set of safety prompts.
09:29 Nina: yes add those as a separate bucket flagged safety; Optimize will run targeted hallucination checks and produce an alert if rate increases above baseline.
09:38 Ethan: quick nit — your console labels a setting 'quant optimism' — what's that exactly?
09:44 Tobias: that toggles the aggressiveness of quant kernel selection: optimistic tries experimental kernels (faster) and conservative sticks to verified kernels. optimistic gives more savings but we recommend prod only after validation.
09:58 Aisha: any known architecture-specific caveats? our model is a 7b architecture but heavily decoder-only, custom head.
10:06 Nina: decoder-only works fine; the main concern is custom heads that are fragile to quantization — we recommend you run per-layer calibration on the head and consider keeping head layers in fp16.
10:18 Ravi: what about mixed precision like INT8 for weights but FP8 activations? seems complex.
10:24 Nina: we have hybrid profiles that mix formats; FP8 activations can give faster compute on some hardware, but availability depends on underlying kernels. Optimize will show compatible hardware and expected gains.
10:36 Maya: on compliance: can the eval logs be redacted? our legal team wants PII scrubbed before anything leaves the VPC.
10:43 Lucas: yes, redaction hooks and hashed tokens are part of Private eval runner. we'll share the integration guide and the redaction schema.
10:53 [short pause]
11:05 Nina: okay, last bit — rollout strategy in console: you can do percent rollouts, canary by user segment or by route, and automatic regression detection. if fidelity drops beyond threshold, console initiates rollback and notifies the release approvers.
11:25 Ethan: how are regressions detected? is it heuristic or model-comparison?
11:31 Nina: both — we compute delta on automated metrics and have optional human-in-the-loop gating. for safety buckets, we default human review at 5% regression.
11:42 Lucas: let's recap actions and next steps. Lucas: send SOC2 + network diagram and pilot worksheet. Nina: produce qprofiles for the three buckets and schedule benchmark window. Polaris: provide prompt sets and confirm compliance contact.
11:58 Aisha: thanks — also can you include sample run logs and a sample sensitivity heatmap exported as CSV?
12:05 Nina: yes will attach.
12:10 Ravi: final question — if we go with FP8-balanced and later switch to int8, how complicated is rollback?
12:16 Nina: rollbacks are straightforward; console records the previous qprofile and model variant. rollback includes clearing cache or warming baseline caches to avoid cold-p99 spikes.
12:28 Lucas: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc bundle and a proposed schedule.
12:34 [meeting ends]
